chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Muhammad ibn 'Amru ibn Sahl from Harun ibn Kharija from Jabir al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever seeks forgiveness of Allah seventy times after the Morning Prayer, Allah will forgive him even if he committed more than seventy thousand sins that day, and whoever commits more than seventy thousand sins, there is no good in him.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for seeking forgiveness seventy times after Fajr prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the specific virtue of post-Fajr *istighfar*, a time when divine mercy is particularly accessible as the day begins. The mention of 'seventy thousand' sins serves as a hyperbolic indicator of Allah's boundless capacity to forgive, reassuring believers that even habitual sinners can attain purification through consistent devotion. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on daily spiritual maintenance and the transformative power of repentance in cleansing the soul before engaging in worldly affairs.
